title: Wooden Joe recording of 1945 and brass band after discharge
summary: He recorded with Wooden Joe in May 1945, left the Navy in August, and played funerals with Bocage's band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I remember about the first time that I remember meeting you and hearing you is when we made those records with Wooden Joe over the...
Yeah, well I was in the Navy then. That's the night I was around in 44, wasn't it?
May of 45. May of 45. When I got out that same year.

And the Navy Dodds was supposed to be there. Be there, yeah. He had his arm or something so they got me there. Yeah, he got me that last minute to come and record. Still had on your uniform, I remember.

Yeah, yeah, it was a night at the old artesian hall, called the Night in New Orleans. I made a recording that night. It was Wooden Joe, they weren't there playing... Yes, Wooden Joe and Burbank and Lawrence. Lawrence and we had Boots playing trombones, playing the bass. Jim Crow playing the trombone. That's right. The night we made it recorded.
And you got out of the Navy then just a few months after that in August.
After that, August in 45, yeah, the show out of the Navy.
Did they still have some of the old onward band at that time? I didn't know they called it that.

Well, that's what I'm thinking now. I placed several parades and funerals with it, but I know it was led by Peter Boccoff over in Algiers. I played lots of funerals with them on that. I think it was called the Onward Brass Band, part of it. Peter might explain it more better.
Yeah, I don't remember that he told us about that particular group.
